summary: The paper addresses efficient text classification, where deep neural models achieve strong accuracy but are slow to train and test. It proposes fastText, a linear model with a rank constraint, bag-of-words/n-gram features, hierarchical softmax, and asynchronous SGD on CPUs. On sentiment and tag-prediction benchmarks fastText is on par with deep-learning classifiers while being orders of magnitude faster; the target AG News test accuracy with h=10 and bigrams is 92.5%.

why: The authors' complete implementation of the exact system claimed is public and cloned: src/ is the C++ fastText whose supervised mode ('./fasttext supervised -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr ...') is precisely the configuration of C1, and the repo ships the authors' own reproduction script for Table 1 (classification-results.sh), which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release (incl. AG News 120k train / 7.6k test) and trains/evaluates every row. No weights are needed (training is from scratch), the paper's hyperparameters (h=10, bigrams, 5 epochs, lr in {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5}, 20 CPU threads) are fully specified, no GPU is required, and the host's 22 CPU cores match the paper's 20-thread CPU setup, so training costs seconds-to-minutes. What remains is environment plumbing rather than missing science: the Linux/POSIX build path and the dataset download. Fallback if the native build cannot be made to work on Windows is to install the same code as a prebuilt wheel (pip fasttext-wheel / fasttext) or, worst case, use the authors' own PyTorch EmbeddingBag fastText model (python/doc/examples/FastTextEmbeddingBag.py) as the training engine, with the caveat that the latter is a re-implementation and would downgrade the verdict to partially_reproduced.

blockers: Host is Windows 11: classification-results.sh is a bash script and the Makefile/`make` path assumes a POSIX shell plus g++/clang++ - neither is guaranteed present; needs MinGW/MSYS2, WSL or CMake+MSVC

setup.py hard-codes '-O3 -funroll-loops -pthread -march=native' extra compile args, which MSVC rejects, so 'pip install .' from source on Windows needs MinGW or a prebuilt wheel (fasttext-wheel) instead
'make' uses -march=native -std=c++17; fine on modern gcc/clang, irrelevant if a wheel is used
No GPU on the host - not a blocker: the paper's fastText rows are CPU-only (20 threads) and AG News trains in ~1 s/epoch
Network access to the dataset download URLs cannot be assumed; a mirror (HF ag_news) plus a short format converter covers this

approach: The paper's exact system is the authors' own fastText C++ supervised trainer, and the repo ships classification-results.sh which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release and trains/evaluates every Table 1 row, so the plan is plumbing rather than re-implementation: get a working fasttext engine, get AG News in `__label__N` format, then run the authors' configuration `-dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20`. A thin reproduce.py drives everything with the Python binding (fasttext-wheel on Windows, native build or `make` when a POSIX toolchain exists), reconstructs the missing validation split (10% of the 120k train set, assumption A4) to pick lr from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, then retrains on the full training set and evaluates on the official 7.6k test set. The same driver also emits the no-bigram C2 row for free. Only results/metrics.json is written by us; all training/eval numbers come from the authors' binary or its official Python binding, and the fallback to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example is explicitly flagged as a re-implementation. Everything is CPU-only with 20 threads, matching the paper.
steps: Environment probe: print python version, os.cpu_count(), total RAM, and shutil.which for make/g++/clang/cmake; confirm the cloned repo path and record `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Read the authors' classification-results.sh and classification-example.sh to copy their exact dataset URLs and argument list for the AG News row; do not edit them. If a POSIX bash + make are available, running classification-results.sh directly is the preferred path and reproduce.py only parses/wraps its output.

Build/find the engine via fasttext_engine.py: try `import fasttext`; else `pip install fasttext-wheel` (prebuilt, Windows-safe); else native `make`/`pip install .`; else fall back to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example and mark the run as a re-implementation.

Download AG News with prepare_data.py (authors' URL first, then Zhang et al. CSV / HF mirror) and convert to `__label__1..4 <tokens>` lines; write data/ag_news.full.train (120k), data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and, with a fixed seed, data/ag_news.train (108k) + data/ag_news.valid (12k).

Smoke test (see smoke_test): train on 2k lines, 1 epoch, dim 10, wordNgrams 2, verify the returned (N, P@1, R@1), verify `test` on the 1k test subset, and verify a stub results/metrics.json round-trips.

Intermediate checks before the full run: line counts 120000/7600 (full train/test) and 108000/12000 (search/valid), 4-class balance printout, label set == {__label__1..4}, vocabulary and bigram-hash collision counts, and a 1-epoch unigram sanity baseline well above the 25% chance level.

lr search: for lr in {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} run the authors' trainer on data/ag_news.train with -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20 -minCount 1, evaluate on data/ag_news.valid, keep all four validation accuracies.

Final C1 run: pick the argmax-lr and retrain on the full 120k data/ag_news.full.train with the same flags, then run the authors' test command on data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and record P@1 as a percentage.
C2 run (cheap): repeat the final training with -wordNgrams 1 at the selected lr and evaluate on data/ag_news.test.

Write results/metrics.json in the contract's shape: {claim_id, dataset, split, metric, value, unit, target_value, tolerance, passed, config_used, lr_search_results, validation_accuracy, test_examples, engine ('fasttext-wheel' | 'native build' | 'EmbeddingBag re-implementation'), git_hash, runtime_seconds} for C1 and a secondary entry for C2.
Report: the C1 accuracy with |acc - 92.5| <= 1.0 pass/fail, the selected lr, the engine provenance, and any deviation entry (e.g., bucket=10M instead of A3's 100M).
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke  ->  builds a 2k-line train / 1k-line test subset from the converted AG News files, trains with dim=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=1, lr=0.1, thread=4 via fasttext_engine.train(), then fasttext_engine.test() on the 1k subset; asserts that both calls return without error, that N matches the subset size, that P@1 is a float in [0,1], and that a stub results/metrics.json is written and reloadable. Runs in well under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Data sizes: data/ag_news.full.train == 120000 lines, data/ag_news.test == 7600 lines, search/valid split from the same 120000 lines (108000/12000) with no overlap (verify by hashing the first token+label of each line).
Class balance: 4 labels, each ~25% in train and test (AG News is exactly balanced); print counts before training.
Label vocabulary: sorted label set equals {__label__1,__label__2,__label__3,__label__4}; no row lacks a label prefix.
Feature sanity: report dictionary word count and the fraction of the 10M bin space probed by bigrams (fastText verbose=2 prints these), and confirm minn=maxn=0 so no character n-grams leak in.

Sanity baseline: unigram fastText (wordNgrams=1, 1 epoch, lr=0.1) on the 108k search set should reach roughly 85-90% on the validation set, comfortably above the 25% chance level; if it is near chance the data conversion (labels/tokens) is wrong.

Engine provenance check: print fasttext module version/`./fasttext --help` banner and assert the model file exists after training; if the EmbeddingBag fallback is used, set verdict_ceiling='partially_reproduced' in metrics.json.
Memory check before the final run: est. input matrix = (|V| + bucket) * dim * 4 bytes; if the 100M-bin variant (A3) would exceed available RAM, stay at bucket=10M and log the deviation.
budget_plan: Of a ~45 min budget: 2 min environment probe + engine setup attempts (extended only if a native build is needed), 1-3 min data download/convert/verify, 1 min smoke test, 2 min intermediate checks plus the unigram baseline, 7-8 min for the 4-point lr grid (4 x 5 epochs on 108k ~ 10-20 s each plus validation eval), ~1 min for the final retrain on 120k and the 7.6k test pass, ~1 min for the no-bigram C2 run, 2-3 min to write results/metrics.json and the report. Total ~15-20 min, leaving >2x margin; the only unbounded step is the toolchain/wheel install, which is capped at 5 min before switching to the EmbeddingBag fallback.

"""Re-create the fastText AG News result of "Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text
Classification" (arXiv 1607.01759), Table 1, using the authors' own fastText
0.9.2 trainer (via its official python binding).

  python reproduce.py            full run: verify data, select lr, train/eval C1 + C2
  python reproduce.py --smoke    2k-line / 1-epoch smoke test only
  python reproduce.py --search   4-point lr grid x 3 seeds on the validation split

Writes results/metrics.json.  All numbers are computed by the authors' code
from data; nothing is copied from the paper.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import statistics
import sys
import time

import config
import fasttext_engine as engine
import prepare_data


def _ensure_data():
    os.makedirs(config.DATA_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    report = prepare_data.prepare()
    return report


def _train_eval(ft, train_path, test_path, word_ngrams, lr, epochs, threads,
                seed=None, verbose=0):
    model = engine.train_supervised(
        ft,
        input=train_path,
        output=os.path.join(config.DATA_DIR, "_model"),  # binding requires -output
        dim=config.DIM,
        lr=lr,
        wordNgrams=word_ngrams,
        minCount=config.MIN_COUNT,
        bucket=config.BUCKET,
        epoch=epochs,
        thread=threads,
        loss=config.LOSS,
        minn=config.MINN,
        maxn=config.MAXN,
        lrUpdateRate=config.LR_UPDATE_RATE,
        label=config.LABEL,
        verbose=verbose,
        seed=seed,
    )
    n, p1, _ = engine.test(model, test_path)
    acc = 100.0 * p1
    labels = sorted(model.get_labels())
    del model
    return {"n": n, "accuracy": acc, "labels": labels,
            "seed_used": seed, "seed_supported": engine.SEED_SUPPORTED}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- smoke
def run_smoke():
    t0 = time.time()
    _ensure_data()
    train_f, test_f = prepare_data.make_smoke_files()
    ft = engine.get_fasttext()
    res = _train_eval(ft, train_f, test_f, word_ngrams=2, lr=0.1, epochs=1,
                      threads=4, seed=1, verbose=2)
    assert res["n"] == config.SMOKE_TEST_LINES, res["n"]
    assert isinstance(res["accuracy"], float) and 0.0 <= res["accuracy"] <= 100.0
    assert res["labels"] == ["__label__1", "__label__2", "__label__3", "__label__4"], res["labels"]
    os.makedirs(config.RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    out = {"smoke": res, "engine": engine.PROVENANCE, "seconds": time.time() - t0}
    with open(os.path.join(config.RESULTS_DIR, "smoke_metrics.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print("[smoke] N=%d P@1=%.4f acc=%.2f%% (%.1fs)" %
          (res["n"], res["accuracy"] / 100.0, res["accuracy"], out["seconds"]))
    print("[smoke] engine:", engine.PROVENANCE)
    print("[smoke] OK -> results/smoke_metrics.json")
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- lr search
def run_search(seeds=config.SEARCH_SEEDS, grid=config.LR_GRID):
    _ensure_data()
    ft = engine.get_fasttext()
    log = {"grid": grid, "seeds": seeds, "points": []}
    for lr in grid:
        accs = []
        for seed in seeds:
            r = _train_eval(ft, config.F_TRAIN, config.F_VALID, word_ngrams=2,
                            lr=lr, epochs=config.EPOCH, threads=config.THREADS,
                            seed=seed)
            accs.append(r["accuracy"])
        mean = statistics.mean(accs)
        log["points"].append({"lr": lr, "valid_accs": accs, "valid_mean": mean})
        print("[search] lr=%-5s valid accs=%s mean=%.2f" % (lr, accs, mean))
    best = max(log["points"], key=lambda p: p["valid_mean"])
    log["selected_lr"] = best["lr"]
    log["selected_valid_mean"] = best["valid_mean"]
    with open(config.SELECTED_CONFIG, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"lr": best["lr"], "selected_on": "validation (12k holdout of train)",
                   "grid": grid, "seeds": seeds,
                   "valid_mean": best["valid_mean"],
                   "points": log["points"]}, f, indent=2)
    print("[search] selected lr=%s (valid mean %.2f)" % (best["lr"], best["valid_mean"]))
    return log


def _load_lr(do_quick_search=True):
    """lr from a previous validation search; otherwise run the paper's grid once."""
    if os.path.isfile(config.SELECTED_CONFIG):
        with open(config.SELECTED_CONFIG) as f:
            sel = json.load(f)
        print("[lr] using saved selection: lr=%s (%s)" % (sel["lr"], sel.get("selected_on")))
        return sel["lr"], sel
    if do_quick_search:
        log = run_search(seeds=[config.SEARCH_SEEDS[0]])
        return log["selected_lr"], log
    print("[lr] no saved selection; using the authors' script lr for ag_news: %s" % config.DEFAULT_LR)
    return config.DEFAULT_LR, {"source": "authors' classification-results.sh", "lr": config.DEFAULT_LR}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- full run
def run_full():

audit_summary: The match target C1 is reproduced on the correct experiment: full 120k-example AG News train, untouched 7,600-line Zhang et al. test split, dim=10, wordNgrams=2, 5 epochs, lr from the paper's {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} grid selected on a 12,000-line train holdout, 20 threads, run through the authors' own fastText 0.9.2 C++ trainer (prebuilt wheel, same source/args as the CLI) rather than a re-implementation. A clean re-run reproduces 92.31 +/- 0.07 (C1) and 91.31 +/- 0.11 (C2), gaps of 0.19 each, well inside the 1.0 tolerance; no number is hard-coded, echoed from the paper, or computed on the wrong split (target constants 92.5/91.5 in config.py feed only the pass/fail band). Two stated fidelity points are only partial: hierarchical softmax (R4/R12) and the 100M-bin hash space (R8) are not used -- the flat softmax and 10M buckets are the authors' own released-script defaults, are disclosed in metrics.json, and are accuracy-neutral at k=4 and 0.03% bin occupancy respectively. The residual 0.19 gap is consistent with run noise and the paper's underspecified lr/tokenization choices (A1, A4, A17), not with an agent error. Nothing was scaled down for the target run (full data, full 5 epochs, 5 repeats vs. the paper's single run); the only limitations are the un-attempted extra datasets and the YFCC100M claim.

requirement_check.evidence: Bag of unigrams+bigrams built via the authors' normalize_text pipeline; wordNgrams=2 in every C1 run (config.py wordNgrams=2, feature_stats shows 340,085 distinct bigrams over a 20k sample).
Delegated to the authors' fastText 0.9.2 C++ trainer (dim=10, supervised), which is exactly the average-embedding + linear-layer architecture of Figure 1.
loss='softmax' over the 4 classes is negative log-likelihood on f(BAx_n); the loss actually optimized by the trainer.

Paper requires hierarchical softmax with a Huffman tree (O(h log k)); the run uses flat softmax (loss='softmax'), disclosed in metrics.json notes. Objective (NLL over 4 classes) is unchanged and the effect at k=4 is accuracy-neutral, but the stated component is not implemented. Test-time binary-heap T-top (R12) also absent.
thread=20 (CPU) and lrUpdateRate=100 gives fastText's linear learning-rate decay.
dim=10, epoch=5, lr grid {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} searched on a 12k holdout; selected lr=0.25 (valid_mean 91.667).
Hyperparameters are held fixed in config.py but only AG News (C1/C2) was executed; Sogou/DBpedia/Yelp/Yahoo/Amazon were not run, so cross-dataset sharing is asserted, not demonstrated.

bucket=10,000,000 (authors' classification-results.sh) instead of the paper's 100M for unigram+bigram; disclosed in A15 and metrics.json notes. Collision rate is negligible (0.034% of bins probed), so accuracy impact ~0, but the literal R8 setting is not used.
Uses the Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release (Google Drive / fast.ai mirror), official 120k train and 7,600 test splits; test class balance 1900x4.
YFCC100M tag-prediction claim (C8) not attempted; the paper's filtered-split release never shipped. Not part of the match target.
thread=20 on CPU for all training runs.
No Huffman-tree prediction or binary-heap T-top exploration; flat softmax with k=1 threshold=0.0, so P@1 == accuracy for single-label data.

divergence_causes: paper_underspecified (A1 lr choice, A4 validation-split construction, A5/A17 tokenization)
